A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe LiRA, its Arca and LaSR components, and the same benchmark suite. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are available and readable enough for reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, sentence-ranking and reasoning experiments, component ablations, and empirical representation analyses in Tables 1–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds model-scale comparisons, training diagnostics and translation-budget experiments, including Tables 11–16.

M1.justification: The stated Arca objective changes from reinforcement learning plus separate cosine-alignment and squared Euclidean anchoring penalties to reinforcement learning plus one cosine anchoring penalty (v1 Equations 5 and 12; v2 Equations 5 and 9). This is a focused objective revision; critic–actor selection and LaSR's queue-based objectives remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BelebeleRetrieval, MLQARetrieval, STS22, MGSM, X-CSQA and LazRetrieval with the same reported language coverage. LazRetrieval-mega remains a companion resource rather than newly evaluated data. Added experiments principally vary models and translator configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds explicit Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and 4B baselines to the LazRetrieval comparison, which previously included only the 8B variant. Other comparator families remain. GTE, BGE and E5-Mistral already appeared as baselines in v1; their new 'with LiRA' rows test adaptations rather than introduce new external methods.

E3.justification: The reasoning tables replace Qwen3-14B with Qwen3-8B. V2 introduces Base/Large/Max configurations, additional embedding backbones, translator-budget experiments and offline/online timing protocols. Table 9 also changes the stated STS22 and Belebele pooling sizes from 5k and 1k to 8 each. These are reported setting changes, without independently establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds cross-backbone and model-scale analyses, epoch-wise anchoring diagnostics, component-level error proxies, translator-budget sensitivity and resource comparisons, plus a translation-artifact case study (Tables 11–16; Appendix C.3). Existing component ablations remain, with revised reasoning results. RKHS estimates, Lipschitz analyses and translator-selection plots were already present in v1.

E5.justification: V1 Section 5.1 explicitly reports ten repetitions and averaging for each experiment; v2 removes this disclosure without providing replacement run or seed counts. Existing descriptive standard deviations and quantiles remain. Table 12's 'mean±std if available' wording is a placeholder, not actual uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: LiRA's public MLQA score changes from 81.66 to 82.01. The LazRetrieval Qwen3-E-8B average changes from 76.78 to 68.05, while the earlier LiRA scores are retained as LiRA-Max. Numerous scaling, diagnostic, budget and timing results are added. Reasoning results are replaced under reported 8B settings: LiRA reports 71.1 on MGSM and 65.5 on X-CSQA, versus 89.2 and 62.0 under the earlier reported 14B settings; these are not same-setting performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Assumption 1 changes anchoring to the observed translation T(x) into anchoring to the ideal translation y*, altering a central premise of the guarantee. Appendix A.2 also replaces its encoder/edit-distance Lipschitz formula with a scorer/representation-distance formula. The bound and proof remain largely unchanged, leaving the revised assumption inconsistent with a retained proof step. The concatenation derivation is moved, not newly added.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly claims plug-and-play applicability across pretrained backbones with lightweight fine-tuning. Its abstract drops v1's specific claim of robustness under few-shot and noise-amplified settings. The central contributions—Arca/LaSR, theoretical stability, the seven-language retrieval resource and strong multilingual performance—remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantial interpretations concerning ideal representations as analytical references, diagnostic evidence for error contraction, backbone scaling and generality, and computation–quality tradeoffs. Appendix C.3 explains how translation meta-text can distort embeddings and critic rewards. Earlier qualifications about empirical bound surrogates and evaluator-family bias are retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: V2 supplies exact translation and critic prompts, named translator/critic configurations, parameter counts, diagnostic embedding computations, and training/inference GPU-hour measurements (Appendices C–D). These substantially expand reproducibility information. Both versions retain prospective GitHub and Hugging Face release statements; the PDFs do not establish newly available code or data access.

R1.justification: V2 adds references such as Haddow et al., Ataman et al., and Beinborn and Choenni, while removing discussion of CORA and some dense-retrieval work. Positioning against MindMerger and Lusifer shifts toward parallel-data dependence and missing low-resource training information. The overall retrieval/reasoning literature scope remains, and bibliographic updates to retained works are not new citations.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, theoretical setup and anchoring explanation. It adds practical-validity and motivation sections, moves the concatenation discussion to Appendix A.3, and reorganizes the appendices into A–D. The dedicated ethics and reproducibility statements disappear.

P2.justification: The main text switches from one column to a two-column format with a recurring ICML template header. Tables 1 and 2 exchange order and gain grouped adaptation rows and parameter information; six new appendix tables appear. Figure 2 changes translator labels, while existing figures are extensively resized and relocated rather than replaced by new analyses.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful evidence about backbone generality and computation budgets, together with substantially better implementation documentation. However, it removes the ten-run averaging disclosure, leaves the revised anchoring assumption unreconciled with the proof, and introduces unexplained differences between LazRetrieval scores in Tables 1 and 12. These gains and unresolved consistency problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
